22900.meaning1: story of the young gentleman Kevaṭṭa
22900.meaning2: the story of the young gentleman Kevaṭṭa

examples.text: seyyathā'pi, bhikkhave, dakkho kevaṭṭo vā kevaṭṭ'antevāsī vā sukhum'acchikena jālena parittaṃ udakadahaṃ otthareyya. tassa evam'assa, ye kho keci imasmiṃ udakadahe oḷārikā pāṇā, sabbe te antojālīkatā.

tena kho pana samayena sātissa nāma bhikkhuno kevaṭṭaputtassa evarūpaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ hoti, tath'āhaṃ bhagavatā dhammaṃ desitaṃ ājānāmi yathā tadev'idaṃ viññāṇaṃ sandhāvati saṃsarati anaññan'ti.

22904.meaning1: completely and utterly; complete and utter; 100%

examples.text: attani ca, bhikkhave, attaniye ca saccato thetato anupalabbhamāne, yam'pi taṃ diṭṭhiṭṭhānaṃ, so loko so attā, so pecca bhavissāmi nicco dhuvo sassato avipariṇāmadhammo, sassatisamaṃ tath'eva ṭhassāmī'ti, nan'āyaṃ, bhikkhave, kevalo paripūro bāladhammo'ti?

22905.meaning1: all; whole lot; altogether; total; entire; complete
22905.synonym: ekanta, ekantagata, ekantigata, kasiṇa, kiṇha, nissesa, sabbanta, sabbāvant

examples.text: rūpā saddā rasā gandhā, phassā dhammā ca kevalā, iṭṭhā kantā manāpā ca, yāvat'atthī'ti vuccati.
evam'etassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti
bindu cūḷāmaṇ'ākāro, niggahītan'ti vuccate, kevalassa-appayogattā, akāro sannidhīyate.

22907.synonym: kasiṇa, kiṇha, nissesa, sakala, sabbanta, sabbāvant
22907.commentary: (SNa) tasmā kevalakappaṃ jetavanan'ti ettha anavasesaṃ samantato jetavanan'ti evam'attho daṭṭhabbo

examples.text: atha kho aññatarā devatā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā ten'upasaṅkami
mañ'hi, bhante, aññatitthiyā sāvakaṃ labhitvā kevalakappaṃ nāḷandaṃ paṭākaṃ parihareyyuṃ, upāli amhākaṃ gahapati sāvakattaṃ upagato'ti.

22908.grammar: ind, adv, comp, acc sg of kevalakappa

examples.text: kuto taṃ, bhante, adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamissati ! āyasmato, bhante, anuruddhassa bāhiyo nāma saddhivihāriko kevalakappaṃ saṅghabhedāya ṭhito. tatr'āyasmā anuruddho na ekavācikam'pi bhaṇitabbaṃ maññatī'ti.

22909.meaning1: altogether complete; completely realized; entirely perfect

examples.text: so dhammaṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāseti

22910.commentary: (MNa) kevalā paripūrā bālabhūmī'ti bālo tīṇi duccaritāni pūretvā niraye nibbattati, tattha pakk'āvasesena manussattaṃ āgato pañcasu nīcakulesu nibbattitvā puna tīṇi duccaritāni pūretvā niraye nibbattatī'ti ayaṃ sakalā paripuṇṇā bālabhūmi.

examples.text: atha kho ayam'eva tato mahantataro kaliggaho yaṃ so bālo kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. ayaṃ, bhikkhave, kevalaparipūrā bālabhūmī'ti.

22911.grammar: ind, adv, acc sg of kevala
22911.synonym: asesato, asesaṃ, ekantaṃ, eva, paripūraṃ, samantaṃ, sādhukaṃ

examples.text: siyā kho pana, bhante, idh'ekaccassa āyasmato evam'assa, kevalaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ nūna ayam'āyasmā nissāya nekkhamm'ādhimutto'ti. na kho pan'etaṃ, bhante, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.

22912.meaning1: mere faith alone; entirely just belief
22912.commentary: (ANa) kevalaṃ saddhāmattakan'ti paṭivedharahitaṃ kevalaṃ paṭivedhapaññāya asammissakaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ.

examples.text: siyā kho pana, bhante, idh'ekaccassa āyasmato evam'assa, kevalaṃsaddhāmattakaṃ nūna ayam'āyasmā nissāya nekkhamm'ādhimutto'ti. na kho pan'etaṃ, bhante, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ.
aññena ca kevalinaṃ mah'esiṃ, khīṇ'āsavaṃ kukkuccavūpasantaṃ, annena pānena upaṭṭhahassu, khettaṃ hi taṃ puññapekkhassa hotī'ti.
ye ca kho keci, bhikkhave, samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā… rūpassa nibbidā virāgā nirodhā anupādā vimuttā, te suvimuttā. ye suvimuttā, te kevalino. ye kevalino vaṭṭaṃ tesaṃ n'atthi paññāpanāya.

22914.grammar: pron, masc & nt instr pl of kaci

examples.text: acchinnacīvaro nāma bhikkhussa cīvaraṃ acchinnaṃ hoti rājūhi vā corehi vā dhuttehi vā, yehi kehici vā acchinnaṃ hoti.

22915.notes: Saddanīti takes this as an independent root kele mamāyane. Some take it as √kīḷ. Edgerton notes under kelāyati, 'probably not connected with Skt. keli, but origin obscure'.

22916.meaning2: cares for, cherishes; treasures; is possessive of
22916.notes: Saddanīti takes this as an independent root kele mamāyane. Some take it as √kīḷ, to play. Edgerton notes under kelāyati, 'probably not connected with Skt. keli, but origin obscure'.

examples.text: yāvakīvañ'ca tesu paṃsv'āgārakesu avigatarāgā honti avigatacchandā avigatapemā avigatapipāsā avigatapariḷāhā avigatataṇhā, tāva tāni paṃsv'āgārakāni allīyanti keḷāyanti dhanāyanti mam'āyan'ti.

ath'assa ten'eva kāraṇena kuṇḍadhānatthero'ti nāmaṃ jātaṃ. so uṭṭhāya samuṭṭhāya tehi kariyamānaṃ keḷiṃ sahituṃ asakkonto ummādaṃ gahetvā tumhe koṇḍā, tumhākaṃ upajjhāyo koṇḍo, ācariyo koṇḍo'ti vadati.

22919.grammar: pron, interr, masc nom sg of ka

examples.text: uṭṭhahatha nisīdatha, ko attho supitena vo, āturānañ'hi kā niddā, sallaviddhāna ruppataṃ.
idha no, āvuso, ko viseso, ko adhippayāso, kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ samaṇassa vā gotamassa amhākaṃ vā, yadidaṃ dhammadesanāya vā dhammadesanaṃ, anusāsaniyā vā anusāsanin'ti?

22920.meaning2: (when repeated) how great a difference there is between A and B!; how far is A from B !; what is the difference between A and B?

22922.meaning2: ko ca (noun)… ko (verb) (an extension of (i)and (ii), where the verb substitutes for a noun, influenced by the sense o/ka as who am I to, who is competent to… ?); how far is one from being able to… ; how unworthy is one to… ; how different is A from him who…

22924.meaning1: what is the name of this (person)?

examples.text: aparaṃ pana ekadivasaṃ uyyānaṃ gacchanto tath'eva devatāhi nimmitaṃ sunivatthaṃ supārutaṃ pabbajitaṃ disvā, ko nām'eso sammā'ti sārathiṃ pucchi.
ko nu hāso kim'ānando, niccaṃ pajjalite sati, andhakārena onaddhā, padīpaṃ na gavesatha.
pubb'eva me, bhikkhave, sambodhā anabhisambuddhassa bodhisattass'eva sato etadahosi, ko nu kho rūpassa assādo, ko ādīnavo, kiṃ nissaraṇaṃ?
ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā'ti?
ko nu kho, bho, pahoti imaṃ mahāpathaviṃ uttarena āyataṃ dakkhiṇena sakaṭamukhaṃ sattadhā samaṃ suvibhattaṃ vibhajitun'ti?

22927.meaning2: not to speak of… , never mind…

22928.meaning1: what to say of; how much more; no need to talk about

examples.text: tañ'ce bhikkhuṃ aññe bhikkhū jāneyyuṃ nisinnapubbaṃ iminā bhikkhunā dvattikkhattuṃ pātimokkhe uddissamāne, ko pana vādo bhiyyo, na ca tassa bhikkhuno aññāṇakena mutti atthi

imesaṃ ce tumhe, bhikkhave, dasannaṃ kathāvatthūnaṃ upādāy'upādāya kathaṃ katheyyātha, imesam'pi candimasūriyānaṃ evaṃmah'iddhikānaṃ evaṃmah'ānubhāvānaṃ tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyeyyātha, ko pana vādo aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānan'ti!
catuppadānan'ti sīhā byagghā dīpi acchā taracchā kokā mahiṃsā hatthī.
padumaṃ yathā kokanadaṃ sugandhaṃ, pāto siyā phullam'avītagandhaṃ, aṅgīrasaṃ passa virocamānaṃ, tapantam'ādiccam'iv'antalikkhe'ti.

22931.commentary: (MNa) kokanado'ti kokanadaṃ vuccati padumaṃ. so ca maṅgalapāsādo olokanakapadumaṃ dassetvā kato, tasmā kokanado'ti saṅkhaṃ labhi.

examples.text: evaṃ me sutaṃ, ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā bhaggesu viharati susumāragire bhesakaḷāvane migadāye. tena kho pana samayena bodhissa rājakumārassa kokanado nāma pāsādo acirakārito hoti anajjhāvuṭṭho samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtena.
atha kho kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ mahāvanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā ten'upasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekam'antaṃ aṭṭhāsi.
idh'āgamā vijjupabhāsavaṇṇā, kokanadā pajjunnassa dhītā, buddhañ'ca dhammañ'ca namassamānā, gāthā'c'imā atthavatī abhāsi.
kokanudo'pi kho paribbājako rattiyā paccūsasamayaṃ paccuṭṭhāya yena tap'odā ten'upasaṅkami gattāni parisiñcituṃ.

22935.meaning1: remains of a wolf kill; wolf's leftovers
22935.meaning2: wolf's leavings, remnants of a wolfs meal

22936.commentary: (SNa) kokāliko bhikkhu yena bhagavā ten'upasaṅkamī'ti, ko ayaṃ kokāliko, kasmā ca upasaṅkami? ayaṃ kira kokālikaraṭṭhe kokālikanagare kokālikaseṭṭhissa putto pabbajitvā pitarā kārāpite vihāre paṭivasati cūḷakokāliko'ti nāmena, na devadattassa sisso. so hi brāhmaṇaputto mahākokāliko nāma.

examples.text: atha kho subrahmā paccekabrahmā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ ārabbha bhagavato santike imaṃ gāthaṃ abhāsi

22941.meaning2: (with opened flowers) like the red lotus

examples.text: mayūrakoñc'ābhirude, kokil'ābhinikūjite, khattiyānaṃ kule bhadde, kiṃ nu sukhataraṃ tato.

tena kho pana samayena rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikāya deviyā saddhiṃ uparipāsādavaragato hoti. atha kho rājā pasenadi kosalo mallikaṃ deviṃ etadavoca, atthi nu kho te, mallike, koc'añño attanā piyataro'ti?

22945.grammar: pron, masc nom sg of kaci

examples.text: yo'dha koci manussesu, parapāṇāni hiṃsati, asmā lokā paramhā ca, ubhayā dhaṃsate naro.
tasmā't'iha, phagguna, tava ce'pi koci sammukhā avaṇṇaṃ bhāseyya, tatrā'pi tvaṃ, phagguna, ye gehasitā chandā ye gehasitā vitakkā te pajaheyyāsi.
atha kho maṃ, bhante, purisā upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ, na kho dāni devassa koci dānaṃ dīyatī'ti.
hirīnisedho puriso, koci lokasmi vijjati, yo nindaṃ apabodheti, asso bhadro kasā'm'iva.

22947.meaning2: etc., someone or other; some or other

examples.text: tato aparena samayena samanuggāhīyamāno vā asamanuggāhīyamāno vā aññabhāgiyañ'c'eva taṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti kocideso lesamatto upādinno, bhikkhu ca dosaṃ patiṭṭhāti, saṅgh'ādiseso.

22949.meaning1: even some; just some; some or other

examples.text: seyyathā'pi, āvuso yamaka, gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo, so ca ārakkhasampanno. tassa koci'd'eva puriso uppajjeyya anatthakāmo ahitakāmo ayogakkhemakāmo jīvitā voropetu'kāmo.
siyā kho pana bhoto rañño mahāyaññaṃ yajamānassa koci'd'eva vippaṭisāro, mahā vata me bhogakkhandho vigacchatī'ti, so bhotā raññā vippaṭisāro na karaṇīyo

22950.meaning1: wickerwork stool; rattan seat; cane stool
22950.commentary: (VIN 2.5.2.4) kocchaṃ nāma vākamayaṃ vā usīramayaṃ vā muñjamayaṃ vā pabbajamayaṃ vā anto saṃveṭhetvā baddhaṃ hoti.

examples.text: yo pana bhikkhu saṅghikaṃ mañcaṃ vā pīṭhaṃ vā bhisiṃ vā kocchaṃ vā ajjhokāse santharitvā vā santharāpetvā vā taṃ pakkamanto n'eva uddhareyya, na uddharāpeyya, anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyya, pācittiyaṃ.
kānanaṃ'va sahitaṃ suropitaṃ, kocchasūcivicit'aggasobhitaṃ, taṃ jarāya viralaṃ tahiṃ tahiṃ, saccavādivacanaṃ anaññathā.
kocchaṃ pasādaṃ añjaniñ'ca, ādāsakañ'ca gaṇhitvā, parikammakārikā viya, sayam'eva patiṃ vibhūsemi.
acaritvā brahmacariyaṃ, aladdhā yobbane dhanaṃ, jiṇṇakoñcā'va jhāyanti, khīṇamacche'va pallale.
mayūra-koñca-abhirutamhi kānane, dīpīhi byagghehi purakkhato vasaṃ, kāye apekkhaṃ jaha mā virādhaya, itissu maṃ citta pure niyuñjasi.

22956.commentary: (APt) gajānaṃ nādo koñcanādo nāma, koñcasakuṇanādasadiso nādo koñcanādo.

examples.text: kiṃnu kho, mahārāja, so hatthī kadāci karahaci koñcanādaṃ nadatī'ti? āma, bhante, nadatī'ti tena hi, mahārāja, so hatthī koñcasakuṇassa sisso'ti?

22957.commentary: (VINa) kāṭakoṭacikāya vā'ti kāṭan'ti purisanimittaṃ, koṭacikā'ti itthinimittaṃ, etehi vā yo akkoso, eso hīno nāma akkoso'ti.

examples.text: hīno nāma akkoso, oṭṭho'si, meṇḍo'si, goṇo'si, gadrabho'si, tiracchānagato'si, nerayiko'si, n'atthi tuyhaṃ sugati, duggati y'eva tuyhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhā'ti, yakārena vā bhakārena vā, kāṭakoṭacikāya vā, eso hīno nāma akkoso.

22961.meaning1: thorny red cotton tree; Bombax ceiba
22961.commentary: (JAa) koṭasimbalī'ti rukkhanāmena devaputtaṃ ālapati. so hi simbalirukkho khandhasākhamahantatāya koṭasimbalināmaṃ labhati, tasmiṃ adhivatthadevaputtassa'pi tadeva nāmaṃ.

examples.text: seyyathā'pi, bhikkhave, ye keci supaṇṇānaṃ rukkhā, koṭasimbali tesaṃ aggam'akkhāyati, evam'eva kho, bhikkhave, ye keci bodhipakkhiyā dhammā, paññ'indriyaṃ tesaṃ aggam'akkhāyati, yadidaṃ, bodhāya. katame ca, bhikkhave, bodhipakkhiyā dhammā?
athimaṃ khuddakaṃ pakkhiṃ, appamaṃsataraṃ mayā, dhārayaṃ byathasi bhītā, kam'atthaṃ koṭasimbali.
koṭisatānaṃ navutīnaṃ, asītiyā'pi ca koṭinaṃ, ete āsuṃ tayo ṭhānā, vimalānaṃ samāgame.
ev'āhaṃ cintayitvāna, n'ekakoṭisataṃ dhanaṃ, nāth'ānāthānaṃ datvāna, himavantam'upāgamiṃ.
anamataggo'yaṃ, bhikkhave, saṃsāro. pubbā koṭi nappaññāyati sattippahārānaṃ asippahārānaṃ usuppahārānaṃ pharasuppahārānaṃ
caṅkamassa anto vā majjhe vā koṭiyaṃ vā rukkhe sati pamādam'āgamma caṅkamantassa nalāṭaṃ vā sīsaṃ vā paṭihaññatī'ti antorukkhatā dutiyo doso.

22965.commentary: (SNa) sattadhā bhinnassa vālassa koṭiyā koṭiṃ paṭivijjheyyā'ti ekaṃ vālaṃ sattadhā bhinditvā, tassa ekaṃ bhedaṃ gahetvā, vātiṅgaṇamajjhe bandhitvā, aparaṃ bhedaṃ kaṇḍassa aggakoṭiyaṃ bandhitvā, usabhamatte ṭhito kaṇḍabaddhāya koṭiyā taṃ vātiṅgaṇabaddhakoṭiṃ paṭivijjheyyā'ti attho.

examples.text: taṃ kiṃ maññasi, ānanda, katamaṃ nu kho dukkarataraṃ vā durabhisambhavataraṃ vā, yo dūrato'va sukhumena tāḷacchiggaḷena asanaṃ atipāteyya poṅkh'ānupoṅkhaṃ avirādhitaṃ, yo vā sattadhā bhinnassa vālassa koṭiyā koṭiṃ paṭivijjheyyā'ti?

ayam'pi ubhato koṭiko pañho tav'ānuppatto, so tayā nibbāhitabbo'ti.
ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā vajjīsu viharati koṭigāme.

22988.meaning2: having caused to pound; having made smash

examples.text: sīghaṃ sīghaṃ atiharāpetvā sīghaṃ sīghaṃ koṭṭāpeyya. sīghaṃ sīghaṃ koṭṭāpetvā sīghaṃ sīghaṃ thusāni uddharāpeyya. evam'assu tāni, bhikkhave, kassakassa gahapatissa dhaññāni aggappattāni sārappattāni suddhāni sāre patiṭṭhitāni.
yā pana bhikkhunī āmakadhaññaṃ viññatvā vā viññāpetvā vā bhajjitvā vā bhajjāpetvā vā koṭṭetvā vā koṭṭāpetvā vā pacitvā vā pacāpetvā vā bhuñjeyya, pācittiyan'ti.
musalāni gahetvāna, dhaññaṃ koṭṭenti māṇavā, puttadārāni posentā, dhanaṃ vindanti māṇavā.

22991.meaning1: having smashed; having pounded; having beaten (something) to a pulp

examples.text: gahapatiko rathā otaritvā kesesu gahetvā nāmetvā kapparapahārehi koṭṭetvā gale gahetvā āgatamaggābhimukhaṃ khipitvā pakkāmi

22992.meaning1: having ground; having crushed; having powdered (something in or with)

examples.text: araṇisahitaṃ dvidhā phālesi, tidhā phālesi, catudhā phālesi, pañcadhā phālesi, dasadhā phālesi, satadhā phālesi, sakalikaṃ sakalikaṃ akāsi, sakalikaṃ sakalikaṃ karitvā udukkhale koṭṭesi, udukkhale koṭṭetvā mahāvāte opuni, app'eva nāma aggiṃ adhigaccheyyan'ti.

taṃ tattha suvānadoṇiyaṃ suvānapiṇḍam'iva dantamusalehi koṭṭetvā jivhāya samparivattiyamānaṃ jivh'āgge tanupasannakheḷo makkheti, vemajjhato paṭṭhāya bahalakheḷo makkheti, dantakaṭṭhena asampattaṭṭhāne dantagūthako makkheti.

araṇisahitaṃ dvidhā phālesi, tidhā phālesi, catudhā phālesi, pañcadhā phālesi, dasadhā phālesi, satadhā phālesi, sakalikaṃ sakalikaṃ akāsi, sakalikaṃ sakalikaṃ karitvā udukkhale koṭṭesi, udukkhale koṭṭetvā mahāvāte opuni, app'eva nāma aggiṃ adhigaccheyyan'ti.
na tesaṃ koṭṭhe openti, na kumbhiṃ na khaḷopiyaṃ, pariniṭṭhitam'esānā, tena me samaṇā piyā.
yehi, bhikkhave, jacc'andhehi hatthissa kāyo diṭṭho ahosi, te evam'āhaṃsu, ediso, deva, hatthī seyyathā'pi koṭṭho'ti.

yaṃ ajjhattaṃ paccattaṃ vāyo vāyogataṃ upādinnaṃ, seyyath'idaṃ, uddhaṅ'gamā vātā, adhogamā vātā, kucchisayā vātā, koṭṭh'āsayā vātā, aṅgam'aṅg'ānusārino vātā, assāso passāso… ayaṃ vuccati, rāhula, ajjhattikā vāyodhātu.

tena kho pana samayena māro pāpimā āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa kucchigato hoti koṭṭham'anupaviṭṭho. atha kho āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa etadahosi, kiṃ nu kho me kucchi garugaro viya mās'ācitaṃ maññe'ti.
ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbakoṭṭhake
